short: ISO 56001:2024 is the ISO requirements standard for an innovation management system, published on 10 September 2024 by ISO/TC 279; it is the certifiable standard in the ISO 56000 family, alongside guidance documents such as ISO 56002.
title: ISO 56001, Innovation Management Systems
subtitle: The ISO requirements standard for an innovation management system, published 2024
body_html:
What ISO 56001 is

ISO 56001 sets the requirements for an innovation management system. In ISO's summary, an organization uses it to develop and demonstrate its capability to innovate, improve its innovation performance and realise value for users, customers and other interested parties. It is written by ISO/TC 279, Innovation management. The first edition was published on 10 September 2024.

Its requirements are generic. ISO says it applies to any organization, of any type or size, whatever it provides and whatever kinds of innovation or approaches it uses.

What it covers

  • Developing and demonstrating innovation capability.
  • Improving innovation performance.
  • Realising value for users, customers and other interested parties.

ISO 56001 is the one requirements standard in the family. ISO/TC 279 also publishes these, all guidance or vocabulary rather than requirements:

  • ISO 56000:2025: Fundamentals and vocabulary. published 2025-01-23 (second edition).
  • ISO 56002:2019: Innovation management system, guidance. published 2019-07-15; being revised (committee draft).
  • ISO 56003:2019: Tools and methods for innovation partnership, guidance. published 2019-02-04; confirmed.
  • ISO 56005:2020: Tools and methods for intellectual property management, guidance. published 2020-11-24; being revised.
  • ISO 56006:2021: Tools and methods for strategic intelligence management, guidance. published 2021-11-19.
  • ISO 56007:2023: Tools and methods for managing opportunities and ideas, guidance. published 2023-08-18.
  • ISO 56008:2024: Tools and methods for innovation operation measurements, guidance. published 2024-04-24.

How conformity is shown

ISO publishes the standard and sells its text. ISO Open Data, the dataset ISO publishes for reuse, records the edition, the committee and the scope, and that is what this page is built from. It does not record who holds a certificate. A certificate against a requirements standard like this one is issued by a certification body after an audit, and it names that body, the edition, the scope and the dates.

What a claim does not mean

A certificate shows an organization runs an audited system for managing innovation. It does not say the organization's products are innovative, and it is not an AI standard: it does not cover how AI systems are built or controlled.

How it relates to ISO/IEC 42001

ISO/IEC 42001 sets requirements for an AI management system. ISO 56001 sets requirements for an innovation management system. Both are management system requirements standards, so an organization can audit them side by side and run them together. In practice the two divide the work: ISO 56001 governs how an organization chooses, tests and scales new ideas, which today often includes new uses of AI, and ISO/IEC 42001 governs how the AI systems it then runs are managed responsibly.

We could not confirm on ISO's own pages whether the two share clause numbering under ISO's common management system structure, because iso.org refuses automated readers. The texts themselves are sold by ISO, so check the clause structure there before planning a combined audit.

ISO 56001 in data centers

ISO 56001 is a business governance standard, not a data center one. Where an operator does publish it, the same checks apply as for any certificate.

  • Scope. A certificate covers named sites, services or activities. One site certified does not mean every site the operator runs is certified.
  • Edition. The certificate names the edition it was audited against.
  • Certification body and certificate number. These let a reader confirm the certificate with the body that issued it.
  • Dates. A certificate has an issue date and an expiry date.

Related standards

It sits with business governance standards on the Standards and Frameworks hub, beside COSO ERM and ISO/IEC 27001, and next to ISO/IEC 42001 for AI.

Primary sources

  • ISO 56001:2024, ISO standard page (linked for readers; iso.org refuses automated readers, so the facts above come from ISO Open Data)
  • ISO 56000:2025
  • ISO 56002:2019
  • ISO/TC 279, Innovation management (committee)
  • ISO Open Data, deliverables metadata: edition, publication date, committee and scope
